title: llmctl gallery
intro:
What llmctl makes on one machine (an AMD Strix Halo, Radeon 8060S, 128 GB unified memory), with the files and settings it was made from. Each example has a **How it was made** block: the models, prompts, seeds and steps read from the file itself, and the ComfyUI graph to make it again.

The [README](https://github.com/chrbayer/AI#readme) is the reference; these pages show results.

sections.title: Scenes from a storyboard
sections.summary: A 20 s scene from one photo: keyframes, four LTX clips, a cut — and what each of seven rounds taught.
sections.intro: `llmctl storyboard plan.json` makes a scene from a photo: keyframes with Qwen-Image Edit, four LTX-2.5 clips through them, checks before and after rendering, and a final video with one soundtrack. The beach scene below is `examples/storyboard.json`; one `--render` makes it (~2 h).

examples.title: The finished scene
examples.text: A woman walks to a shell lying in the sand, picks it up, holds it to her ear and listens; the close-up rises out of the wide shot in a 0.75 s dissolve, and she listens on, opens her eyes and smiles. 20 s, rendered from the plan alone: the chain, then clip 4 with a guide picture in its middle. The sound is one track of surf and wind from Stable Audio, not LTX's per clip.

facts.Checks: no jump, halt or freeze (`llmctl videocheck`), no ghost (vision check every 0.5 s)

examples.command:
llmctl start comfy 9
llmctl storyboard examples/storyboard.json --render

examples.title: The same scene to a song
examples.text: `"soundtrack": "song.flac"` lays a song under the storyboard instead of the ambience: one continuous scene to music. The song is a 30 s instrumental from Stable Audio 3 (guitar, piano, strings).

media.caption: The song alone (Stable Audio 3, 30 s, made in ~10 s)

examples.title: Keyframes
examples.text: Every keyframe is edited from the photo (or from the keyframe before, where the person must stay in place) with Qwen-Image Edit Turbo. The shell is pasted in at one fixed place until it is picked up; a vision model and SAM 3 check positions and sizes before an hour of rendering.

media.caption: The photo it starts from (Z-Image Turbo)
The contact sheet of the final keyframes
Round 1: a shell 'the size of a hand' came out a giant conch

examples.title: Seven rounds, and what each taught
examples.text:
Each version fixed what the one before showed:

1. **v1** — a giant shell, picked up, put down again, picked up: the keyframe after an action was a moment inside it.
2. **v2** — resting-state keyframes, a small shell; at pull 0.5 a ghost at every clip's end.
3. **v3** — the shell pasted in where it lies, pull 0.7: every clip reaches its keyframe; a stall before 10 s.
4. **v4** — clip lengths of their own; clip 3 had her walk back where she did not face, and LTX dissolved her there.
5. **v5** — "brushes the sand off" became a sand fountain with a small figure floating out of it.
6. **v6** — clean of ghosts and jumps; the sea did not move.
7. **v7** — other waves in every keyframe: the sea moves.

media.caption: v2 — ghosts at the clip ends
v4 — dissolved instead of walked (10.5–12.5 s)
v6 — clean, but the sea stands still

examples.title: How hard to pull a clip to its keyframe
examples.text: Clip 1 three times, the walk to the shell, with *Stärke Zielbild* 0.5, 0.7 and 1.0. At 0.5 she rocks in place and jumps to the end picture in its last frame; at 0.7 she walks there and stands still for 1.2 s; at 1.0 the shell flies in through the air. The shell moved at all because Qwen had drawn it elsewhere in each keyframe — hence pasting it in.

examples.title: Why the sea stood still
examples.text: Edited from one photo, every keyframe had the same sea to the pixel, and LTX kept it still between them (0.1–0.3 of change a frame against 1.0–1.3 in a plain clip). Asking each edit for other waves raised it to 0.4–0.55, and the sand at her feet calmed down too.

media.caption: Other waves in the end keyframe

sections.title: A music video
sections.summary: A song, a singer in three shots, lip-synced section by section with LTX-2.5.
sections.intro: `llmctl musicvideo song.flac shot1.png shot2.png ...` cuts a song into sections, has the pictures sing each with LTX-2.5 Talking, cuts every clip to exactly the frames of its section and lays the whole song underneath — so the lips stay on the sound from the first frame to the last.

examples.title: 30 s of German synthpop
examples.text: The song from ACE-Step 1.5 XL; the singer from Z-Image, two more shots of the same person from Qwen-Image Edit (every one from the original, never an edit of an edit). Six sections of 5 s, the shots taking turns; ~6.5 min a section, ~40 min in all. The lips follow the singing; close-ups follow better than head-and-shoulders.
examples.command: llmctl musicvideo song.flac shot0.png shot1.png shot2.png --out musikvideo.mp4

examples.title: Making one, step by step
examples.text:
The music video above, made again from nothing. Every step runs on the same machine; ComfyUI on slot 9, its image API (`--proxy`) on port 8089.

1. **The song.** ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo through llmctl's `/v1/audio/music`: style tags, lyrics with `[Verse]`/`[Chorus]`, tempo, key and language. 30 s in ~20 s.
2. **The singer.** One picture with Z-Image Turbo: a close-up, the face filling much of the frame, 16:9 like the video.
3. **More shots of the same person.** Qwen-Image Edit Turbo, every one edited from that first picture (an edit of an edit gathers noise): a medium shot at a microphone stand, a profile with eyes closed.
4. **The sections.** Without a file the pictures take turns; with one (`--sections`, see `examples/musicvideo.sections`) each section gets its shot and its own prompt, or plays a scene instead of singing.
5. **Look before rendering.** `--dry-run` shows the plan and the time it will take; then the render, ~6.5 min per 5 s section. Finished sections are kept beside the output, so a run that stops, or one with a few lines changed, renders only what is missing.
examples.command:
# 1. the song (the image API of the ComfyUI slot)
curl -s localhost:8089/v1/audio/music -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -o song.mp3 -d '{
  "model": "ace-step-15-xl-turbo", "duration": 30, "language": "de", "bpm": 112, "key": "A minor",
  "prompt": "German synth pop, catchy, 112 BPM, warm female lead vocals, punchy drums, shimmering synths, bright chorus",
  "lyrics": "[Verse]\nIch lauf durch die Straßen, die Lichter gehen an\nDie Stadt hält den Atem, die Nacht fängt an\n\n[Chorus]\nUnd wir tanzen, tanzen bis der Morgen kommt\nUnd wir singen, singen bis die Sonne brennt"}'

# 2.–3. the shots: Z-Image Turbo T2I, then Qwen-Image 2.1 Edit Turbo from it (prompts below)

# 4.–5. the video
llmctl musicvideo song.mp3 shot0.png shot1.png shot2.png --sections examples/musicvideo.sections --dry-run
llmctl musicvideo song.mp3 shot0.png shot1.png shot2.png --sections examples/musicvideo.sections

examples.title: What makes it work
examples.text:
- **Close-ups for lines with many words.** With the face filling the frame the lips follow the singing closely; at head-and-shoulders they drift.
- **Wider shots and profiles for the chorus** and for long notes, where the mouth matters less.
- **Scenes for instrumental parts** (`scene: …` in the sections file): no singing, the song goes on underneath.
- **Every shot from the first picture.** The same face in every section; an edit of an edit drifts and gathers grain.
- **`--continuous`** starts each section on the last frame of the one before: one continuous take, but the face drifts a little with every section. For a story to a song without lip sync, a storyboard with the song as `"soundtrack"` keeps the person the same over far more seconds.
- **The song stays the song.** The video's sound is the original track, not LTX's: the picture is cut to the song's frames, never the other way round.

sections.title: Video
sections.summary: LTX-2.5: a picture or a prompt to a clip with its sound, first to last frame, talking pictures.
sections.intro: ComfyUI's LTX-2.5 templates (int8, distilled), set up and measured by llmctl. 5 s at 1280×704 with sound in 7–15 min.

examples.title: A picture to a clip
examples.text: `LTX-2.5 Video`: the beach photo set in motion, wind and surf as its sound. 409 s.

examples.title: A prompt alone
examples.text: *Switch to Text to Video?* on: a tram in a rainy street, from text alone. 450 s.

examples.title: From a first to a last picture
examples.text: `LTX-2.5 First-Last Frame`: the clip runs from one picture to another — the most natural movement of the three. 895 s. Below it the same clip at 48 fps, frames put between by FILM in 64 s.

examples.title: A picture that speaks
examples.text: `LTX-2.5 Talking`: a voice (Qwen3-TTS) held fixed in LTX's audio latent while the video is made to it; padded to whole frames, the lips stop with the voice.

examples.title: A clip made larger and sharper
examples.text: SeedVR2 3B Video Upscale: the 5 s beach clip from 1280×704 to 1920×1056 with real detail in hair, coat and surf, not just a softer enlargement. Slow here: 2864 s for the five seconds, with *Split Latent* on.

sections.title: Pictures
sections.summary: Z-Image Turbo, Qwen-Image 2.1, FLUX.2 — making, editing, comparing.
sections.intro: ComfyUI's image models as llmctl sets them up, most of them also behind its OpenAI-style image API.

examples.title: Z-Image Turbo
examples.text: 8 steps, a 1024² picture in seconds; the source of most photos on these pages.

examples.title: Qwen-Image 2.1
examples.text: 14 steps (dpmpp_2m) at 1024²: an editorial portrait, a hedgehog in morning mist.

examples.title: One fox, three models
examples.text: A fox in the snow from Qwen-Image 2.1 and from FLUX.2 klein 9B, and the Qwen one sharpened 2× with SeedVR2. Each picture's prompt is in its How it was made block.

examples.title: Samplers and steps
examples.text: The fox with dpmpp_2m at 14 steps and euler at 14 and 25 steps, side by side; the sampler and step count of each are in its How it was made block.

examples.title: Editing: a shirt from a second picture
examples.text: FLUX.2 klein 9B Edit: the denim shirt from one picture put on the person in another; pose, face and light kept.

examples.title: Lettering, and the text encoder's precision
examples.text: A shop window with a sign and a chalkboard in German, from Qwen-Image 2.1 with its Qwen3-VL 8B text encoder at bf16, at w4a8 and as an uncensored ('heretic') version: the lettering came out readable in each.

examples.title: Control: edges, depth, pose
examples.text: A photo steers a new picture: its edges (Canny), its depth or the pose of the person in it, read by a preprocessor inside the workflow. 39–66 s each with the 4- and 8-step Turbo models.

media.caption: Canny: the same lines, a winter beach (Qwen-Image 2.1 Canny Control Turbo)
Depth: a ceramic fox in the same pose (Z-Image Turbo Depth Control)
Pose: another singer, the same pose (Qwen-Image 2.1 Pose Control Turbo)

examples.title: Inpainting and outpainting
examples.text: Inpainting redraws what is masked — here the coat, its mask from SAM 3 ("the dark coat"), transparent in the picture loaded. Outpainting extends a picture beyond its edges, 256 px each side. 42 and 30 s with the Turbo models.

media.caption: A red coat (Qwen-Image 2.1 Inpaint Crop Turbo)
The photo extended to both sides (Qwen-Image 2.1 Outpaint Turbo)

examples.title: Colour for a black-and-white photo
examples.text: The singer's medium shot turned grey, then coloured again by Qwen-Image 2.1 Colorize Turbo in 27 s — with the original to compare.

examples.title: The background removed
examples.text: BiRefNet cuts the subject free in 3 s and keeps the rest transparent (MIT licence).

examples.title: Larger and sharper
examples.text: Z-Image Turbo 2K Upscale: the hedgehog from 1024² to 2048², redrawn lightly (5 steps, denoise 0.33) for detail, in 108 s.

examples.title: Faces and hands mended
examples.text: A group photo from Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo, seven people with faces of about 40 px; two of them came out melted. The FLUX.2 klein 9B Detailer finds each face and hand (YOLO), outlines it with SAM, repaints it at up to 1024 px and pastes it back: both faces are faces again, the others keep who they are, the waving hands get their fingers. 294 s for 7 faces and 10 hands. The Qwen-Image 2.1 Detailer left these faces as they were — a bug in its mask, now fixed, and even then it repaints a melted small face melted.

media.caption: The faces, twice the size: before above, after below
Hands on the left: before above, after below

sections.title: Darkroom: photos from the phone
sections.summary: Every action of the phone page, with an example and tips — German and English
sections.intro: `llmctl darkroom` is a page for the phone in front of ComfyUI: pick or take a photo, tap what should happen, compare before and after, save it to the phone — or make a picture from words. Every example here ran through the page; the times are this machine's (Strix Halo), the first job after a pause takes longer while the model loads. The page speaks German and English.

de.title: Darkroom: Fotos vom Handy
de.summary: Jede Aktion der Handy-Seite, mit Beispiel und Tipps
de.intro: `llmctl darkroom` ist eine Seite fürs Handy vor ComfyUI: Foto wählen oder aufnehmen, antippen, was passieren soll, vorher und nachher vergleichen, aufs Handy sichern — oder ein Bild aus Worten machen. Jedes Beispiel hier lief über die Seite; die Zeiten sind die dieses Rechners (Strix Halo), der erste Auftrag nach einer Pause dauert länger, weil das Modell lädt. Die Seite spricht Deutsch und Englisch.

examples.title: Colorize
examples.text: A black-and-white photo in colour: Qwen-Image 2.1 Colorize, 26 s fast. Colours can be named in the text ("blue sky, green trees"); they apply to the whole picture. More: [the gallery](https://chrbayer.github.io/AI/images.html#colorize).

de.title: Kolorieren
de.text: Ein Schwarzweißfoto in Farbe: Qwen-Image 2.1 Colorize, 26 s schnell. Farben kann man im Text vorgeben („blue sky, green trees“); sie wirken aufs ganze Bild. Mehr: [Galerie](https://chrbayer.github.io/AI/images.html#colorize).

examples.title: Restore
examples.text: Scratches, dust, stains, creases and noise away, the people and the composition kept: Qwen-Image Edit with a restoring prompt, 59 s. This wedding photo was made damaged on purpose — Z-Image Turbo drew the fold and the water stains, a script added dust and scratches — and came back clean, both faces the same. Best on a scan or a photo of the print taken straight on; colour it afterwards with *Edit further* → *Colorize*.

de.title: Restaurieren
de.text: Kratzer, Staub, Flecken, Knicke und Rauschen weg, Personen und Bildaufbau bleiben: Qwen-Image Edit mit einem Restaurier-Prompt, 59 s. Dieses Hochzeitsfoto wurde absichtlich beschädigt erzeugt — Z-Image Turbo malte die Knickfalte und die Wasserflecken, ein Skript fügte Staub und Kratzer hinzu — und kam sauber zurück, beide Gesichter dieselben. Am besten mit einem Scan oder einem gerade abfotografierten Abzug; danach über *Weiter bearbeiten* → *Kolorieren* in Farbe.

media.caption: The faces, twice the size: before above, after below
media.caption_de: Die Gesichter, doppelt so groß: oben vorher, unten nachher

examples.title: Faces
examples.text: Faces and hands found (YOLO), outlined and redrawn at full resolution, then pasted back — for group photos whose small faces came out soft or melted. Seven people: 526 s, the time grows with each face and hand. *Thorough* uses FLUX.2 klein, better on very small faces. A harder case: [the gallery](https://chrbayer.github.io/AI/images.html#detailer).

de.title: Gesichter
de.text: Gesichter und Hände werden gefunden (YOLO), umrissen, in voller Auflösung neu gezeichnet und zurückgesetzt — für Gruppenfotos mit weichen oder zerlaufenen kleinen Gesichtern. Sieben Personen: 526 s, die Zeit wächst mit jedem Gesicht und jeder Hand. *Gründlich* nimmt FLUX.2 klein, besser bei sehr kleinen Gesichtern. Ein schwierigerer Fall: [Galerie](https://chrbayer.github.io/AI/images.html#detailer).

examples.title: Upscale
examples.text: Four times the size, sharper: SeedVR2 7B, the picture brought to 1024 px first. 512 px → 2048 px in 34 s.

de.title: Vergrößern
de.text: Viermal so groß und schärfer: SeedVR2 7B, das Bild vorher auf 1024 px gebracht. 512 px → 2048 px in 34 s.

examples.title: Remove background
examples.text: The background gone, the person on transparency (PNG, shown here as a checkerboard): BiRefNet, 3 s. *Thorough* uses BiRefNet Matting, finer at hair.

de.title: Freistellen
de.text: Der Hintergrund weg, die Person auf Transparenz (PNG, hier als Schachbrett): BiRefNet, 3 s. *Gründlich* nimmt BiRefNet Matting, feiner an Haaren.

examples.title: Erase
examples.text: Name what should go: "the power lines and pylons" — gone, the sky filled in, 65 s. An instruction to Qwen-Image Edit, no marking needed. Works for people in the background, cars, signs, bins; the templates under *Clean up* have the usual ones.

de.title: Entfernen
de.text: Nennen, was weg soll: „die Stromleitungen und Strommasten“ — weg, der Himmel ergänzt, 65 s. Eine Anweisung an Qwen-Image Edit, ohne Markieren. Klappt für Passanten, Autos, Schilder, Mülltonnen; die Vorlagen unter *Aufräumen* haben die üblichen.

examples.title: Edit
examples.text: In one's own words: "Make it a winter day: fresh snow on the street, the roofs and the cars …", 66 s with Qwen-Image Edit Turbo. End with "everything else stays exactly the same" to keep the rest. With a second photo as *picture 2*: say plainly what comes from which — asked for an outfit, the model once took the whole person.

de.title: Ändern
de.text: In eigenen Worten: „Mach daraus einen Wintertag: frischer Schnee auf der Straße, den Dächern und den Autos …“, 66 s mit Qwen-Image Edit Turbo. Mit „Alles andere bleibt genau gleich“ am Ende bleibt der Rest. Mit einem zweiten Foto als *Bild 2*: klar sagen, was woher kommt — nach dem Outfit gefragt, nahm das Modell einmal die ganze Person.

examples.title: Expand
examples.text: More picture around it — left and right, above and below, above only, or all round — the scene continued: 40 s, here above and below. A text is optional; if written, describe the whole scene, not only the new part.

de.title: Erweitern
de.text: Mehr Bild drumherum — links und rechts, oben und unten, nur oben oder rundum — die Szene fortgesetzt: 40 s, hier oben und unten. Ein Text ist optional; wenn, dann die ganze Szene beschreiben, nicht nur das Neue.

examples.title: Paint over
examples.text: Mark a spot with a finger and say what goes there: "a red Hawaiian shirt with white flowers", 26 s. *Keep shape* kept the shirt's cut and folds — mark all of the thing for it. **Name the whole thing**: "red" alone left a grey hat grey; "a red hat" made it red.

de.title: Übermalen
de.text: Eine Stelle mit dem Finger markieren und sagen, was hin soll: „ein rotes Hawaiihemd mit weißen Blüten“, 26 s. *Form behalten* behielt Schnitt und Falten des Shirts — dafür das Ding ganz markieren. **Das Ding ganz nennen**: „rot“ allein ließ einen grauen Hut grau; „ein roter Hut“ machte ihn rot.

examples.title: Cut out
examples.text: One named thing alone on transparency: "the dog", 120 s (Qwen-Image Layered Control). Unlike *Remove background* it takes what is named, not what is in front.

de.title: Ausschneiden
de.text: Ein benanntes Ding allein auf Transparenz: „der Hund“, 120 s (Qwen-Image Layered Control). Anders als *Freistellen* nimmt es das Genannte, nicht das, was vorne steht.

examples.title: Copy pose
examples.text: Someone else, standing exactly the same way: the pose read from the photo (DWPose), "a knight in silver armour in a misty forest" painted on it, 45 s. Describe person and place in full.

de.title: Pose übernehmen
de.text: Jemand anderes in genau derselben Haltung: die Pose aus dem Foto gelesen (DWPose), darauf „ein Ritter in silberner Rüstung in einem nebligen Wald“, 45 s. Person und Ort ganz beschreiben.

examples.title: Redesign
examples.text: The same room, the furniture where it was, in another style: the depth of the photo kept, the rest from the text, 31 s. **Describe materials, colours and light**: "as an alpine cabin" alone only made the room darker; "wooden walls, beamed ceiling, fireplace, red rugs, sheepskins, warm light" made the cabin. The page says so while the text is shorter than five words.

de.title: Neu gestalten
de.text: Derselbe Raum, die Möbel an ihrem Platz, in anderem Stil: die Tiefe des Fotos bleibt, der Rest kommt aus dem Text, 31 s. **Materialien, Farben und Licht nennen**: „als Almhütte“ allein machte den Raum nur dunkler; „Holzwände, Balkendecke, Kamin, rote Teppiche, Lammfelle, warmes Licht“ machte die Hütte. Die Seite sagt das, solange der Text kürzer als fünf Wörter ist.

examples.title: As artwork
examples.text: The photo as watercolour, pencil drawing, oil painting, comic or anime — the people, their faces and the colours kept: Qwen-Image Edit, 58 s, here as a comic. A text is optional ("like a children's book").

de.title: Als Kunstwerk
de.text: Das Foto als Aquarell, Bleistiftzeichnung, Ölgemälde, Comic oder Anime — Personen, Gesichter und Farben bleiben: Qwen-Image Edit, 58 s, hier als Comic. Ein Text ist optional („wie in einem Kinderbuch“).

examples.title: Variants
examples.text: Where one's own words steer the result, *Variants* 1–3 makes as many, one after the other, each with another seed — keep the best. The same sunset twice: 46 and 18 s.

de.title: Varianten
de.text: Wo die eigenen Worte das Ergebnis bestimmen, macht *Varianten* 1–3 so viele, nacheinander, jede mit anderem Zufall — die beste behalten. Derselbe Sonnenuntergang zweimal: 46 und 18 s.

examples.title: Animate
examples.text: A clip of 3, 5 or 8 s with sound: "the waves roll onto the beach, the dog wags its tail", 5 s in 114 s (*Fast*: LTX-2.5's first stage, half the size; *Thorough* both stages, about 6 min). With a second photo the clip runs from the first to it.

de.title: Animieren
de.text: Ein Clip von 3, 5 oder 8 s mit Ton: „die Wellen rollen an den Strand, der Hund wedelt mit dem Schwanz“, 5 s in 114 s (*Schnell*: die erste Stufe von LTX-2.5, halbe Größe; *Gründlich* beide Stufen, etwa 6 min). Mit einem zweiten Foto läuft der Clip vom ersten zu ihm.

examples.title: Make it talk
examples.text: The photo speaks a recording made on the phone (up to 10 s), the clip as long as the voice: 153 s for 8.5 s, *Fast*. A face that fills the picture works best.

de.title: Sprechen lassen
de.text: Das Foto spricht eine Aufnahme vom Handy (bis 10 s), der Clip so lang wie die Stimme: 153 s für 8,5 s, *Schnell*. Ein Gesicht, das das Bild füllt, klappt am besten.

examples.title: Create
examples.text: A picture from words, no photo needed: six models from fast (Z-Image Turbo, 20 s) to best (FLUX.2 dev, ~5 min); Qwen-Image for lettering, umlauts right — this postcard 41 s. LTX-2.5 makes a clip from words. Compared in [the gallery](https://chrbayer.github.io/AI/images.html#fox).

de.title: Erzeugen
de.text: Ein Bild aus Worten, ohne Foto: sechs Modelle von schnell (Z-Image Turbo, 20 s) bis beste Qualität (FLUX.2 dev, ~5 min); Qwen-Image für Schrift, mit richtigen Umlauten — diese Postkarte 41 s. LTX-2.5 macht einen Clip aus Worten. Verglichen in der [Galerie](https://chrbayer.github.io/AI/images.html#fox).

examples.title: Find flaws and repair
examples.text: A picture from *Create* has *Find flaws*: a vision model looks for broken hands, faces and text and marks them — here: fused fingers on one hand, an over-long index finger on the other (183 s, the model started and stopped for it). Untick what is fine, edit the fix, *Repair*: 71 s, *Thorough*.

de.title: Fehler suchen und reparieren
de.text: Ein Bild aus *Erzeugen* hat *Fehler suchen*: ein Vision-Modell sucht kaputte Hände, Gesichter und Schrift und markiert sie — hier: verwachsene Finger an der einen Hand, ein zu langer Zeigefinger an der anderen (183 s, das Modell dafür gestartet und wieder gestoppt). Abwählen, was gesund ist, die Korrektur anpassen, *Reparieren*: 71 s, *Gründlich*.

examples.title: Templates, cancel, zoom, notifications
examples.text:
- **Templates** beside each text field: about 70 tried prompts — weather and light, seasons, clean-up, people, backgrounds, rooms, new scenes, video, cards and logos — searchable; a `[placeholder]` is selected to type over. *Save* keeps one's own, for phone and desk alike.
- **Cancel** stops a waiting or running job within seconds.
- **Zoom**: two fingers up to 4×, a double tap 2.5×.
- **Notify me when done**: a push when a job ends, also with the screen locked (on an iPhone: from the home screen).
- **The history** keeps the last 100 results on the server; *Edit further* takes a result on — restored, then coloured, then enlarged.

de.title: Vorlagen, Abbrechen, Zoom, Benachrichtigungen
de.text:
- **Vorlagen** neben jedem Textfeld: rund 70 erprobte Texte — Wetter und Licht, Jahreszeiten, Aufräumen, Personen, Hintergründe, Räume, neue Szenen, Video, Karten und Logos — durchsuchbar; ein `[Platzhalter]` ist zum Überschreiben markiert. *Speichern* behält eigene, für Handy und Rechner gleich.
- **Abbrechen** stoppt einen wartenden oder laufenden Auftrag in Sekunden.
- **Zoom**: zwei Finger bis 4×, Doppeltippen 2,5×.
- **Benachrichtigen, wenn fertig**: eine Push-Nachricht, wenn ein Auftrag fertig ist, auch bei gesperrtem Bildschirm (auf dem iPhone: vom Home-Bildschirm aus).
- **Der Verlauf** behält die letzten 100 Ergebnisse auf dem Server; *Weiter bearbeiten* nimmt ein Ergebnis mit — restauriert, dann koloriert, dann vergrößert.

sections.title: Music and sound
sections.summary: ACE-Step songs in German and English, YuE2, Stable Audio, voices.
sections.intro: ComfyUI's music templates, also behind llmctl's `/v1/audio/music`. The same lyrics and styles through each.

examples.title: ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo
examples.text: A German pop ballad, an English indie rock song and an orchestral instrumental; ~19 s for 30 s of song.

examples.title: YuE2

sections.summary: Pixal3D and TRELLIS.2: a photo to a textured mesh.
sections.intro: `Pixal3D TRELLIS.2 Image to Model (int8)`: the background cut away, the shape and colours built as voxels, meshed, decimated to 200,000 triangles and baked into 4096 px textures. Drag to turn. On these public pages the models are made small for the web (40,000 triangles, 1024 px textures, ~1 MB); the originals have 200,000 triangles and 4096 px textures.

examples.title: Every model on this machine, dense against MoE
examples.text: `llmctl bench` on llama.cpp v0.6.0 (Vulkan b11429, ROCm b1340), pp512 and tg128 in tokens per second, flash attention on, the machine otherwise idle (2026-10-07). Decode is bound by the memory bandwidth: a dense model reads all its weights for every token, a MoE model only its active experts — so the MoE models decode 5–13× faster than dense ones of their size, and Kolibri-1 with 78B weights decodes faster than an 8B dense model. Vulkan beats ROCm almost everywhere, except Scout. Kolibri runs on its own patched build (Vulkan only).
